content:
<@&857649635274915900>  Week 17 is here and only few weeks left in the cohort!  

I am sorry I have been less available last week, I have been attending 2 conferences in a week and had to be less online. I am fully back now and will respond to everything. And we are continuing with our calls! 

Join our standup starting very soon to give and hear some updates. And more importantly, join us for the last AMA in our Office Hours! This Wednesday we will have our last guest for an AMA session, Nixo who coordinates ACD. https://github.com/eth-protocol-fellows/cohort-seven/issues/489

For following Office Hours, we will host presentations from fellows who are not attending Devcon. This is your final presentation that covers what you worked on so if you cannot make it in person, please sign up for next week or the week after (21 and 28 Oct are dates we have reserved for this) https://github.com/eth-protocol-fellows/cohort-seven/issues/490

author: tmiychao
content:
Further, he is a guide on what is expected from you by the end of the cohort. Please take some time to read it https://notes.ethereum.org/@MarioHavel/cohort7final 
As we mentioned before, fellows are supposed to prepare final presentation and report by end of the cohort. Those coming to Devcon will present at EPF Day there and everyone else will have a chance to present at last Office Hours calls on Oct 21 and Oct 28  (sign up in the issue). You can also record your presentation locally and share the recording if you cannot make it live in neither case. 

Apart from the presentation, there is the final report which we expect from everyone who participated in the cohort. This is not just a one more dev update but more comprehensive report on your work during the entire time, current state of the project and future plans. Check the guide for structure and details.  Please take your time to reflect and write it properly, from your heart not llm. The deadline is end of the month, before leaving for Devcon. 

For both final report and presentation, keep in mind who is your audience. It's meant for mentors, people learning about your work and future fellows - don't spend it on explaining some part of the protocol but focus on your actual work. It will represent your work on the protocol going forward, a single stop to understand what you did, make sure it's comprehensive and focuses on right things. 

If you need feedback or have any questions, please reach out! Join the standup today if want to chat about something as well! Looking forward to see all the cool outcomes 🙂
